subject: Single Record User Control generated by the Microsoft Visual Basic 6.0 Data Object Wizard (a bound data-entry form over a sample Person table)
creator: Microsoft Corporation
title: Figure 16. Single Record User Control, in "Developing Applications with the Microsoft Visual Basic 6.0 Data Object Wizard"
publisher: Microsoft Corporation (MSDN technical article; now served by the Microsoft Learn previous-versions archive)
depicted_event_date: unknown; the capture was made for the article, so no later than its December 1998 publication. No separate capture date is stated.
access_method: Anonymous HTTPS GET with curl; no account, cookie banner, terms click-through, CAPTCHA, or paywall. HTTP 200.
version_model_evidence: Article title names the product and version: Microsoft Visual Basic 6.0 Data Object Wizard.

Article text says the DOW is a Visual Basic add-in that generates data Classes and User Controls, and that a Single Record User Control shows one row in TextBoxes, ComboBoxes and CheckBoxes. The figure shows exactly that.
The figure caption on the page is "Figure 16. Single Record User Control", introduced by the sentence "A DOW-generated Single Record User Control:".

Field names in the figure (PersonID, FirstName, LastName, CountyDescr, CompanyCarDescr, HireDate, ManagerName, Salary, LaborClassCode, MailCheck, Comment) match the article's own GetPerson/GetCounty/GetCompanyCar/GetManager sample stored procedures, tying the figure to this article rather than to an unrelated screenshot.
Classic Windows 9x/NT 4 control rendering (3-D sunken text boxes, gray face, drop-down combo with scrollbar).
displayed_data: Sample data only. Person record 8 is "Peter Rabbit" with salary 31000, labor class 0.234, comment "Comment 8"; the open combo lists US state/county names (Arizona Maricopa, Pima, Yuma; Washington Franklin, King, Pierce, Snohomish, Yakima). The article presents these as a sample schema. No real private person is identifiable.
what_it_is_not: Not the PowerBuilder DataWindow used elsewhere in the project.
Not a full window: Microsoft published the user control's client area only, with no title bar. The published figure is kept whole.
Not VB3/VB4. It is VB6-era (1998) classic Visual Basic.
Not an end-user-written business application. It is Microsoft's own documentation example of wizard-generated VB data-entry UI.
transformations: source/original.gif: none (byte-identical to the HTTP response body).

exports/editorial-frame.png: first GIF frame converted to RGB, scaled uniformly 2x with nearest-neighbour sampling to 668x722, centred at (626,179) on a 1920x1080 #008080 ground. No crop, no retouching, no added text. Command in qa.md.
qa/editorial-frame-720p.png: Lanczos downscale of the export to 1280x720, QA proof only.
